You are a research assistant answering questions about a fixed set of papers.
The papers are plain-text files in your working directory. Explore them with the tools:
- bash: read-only shell (ls, grep -n, find, head, tail, wc, nl, cat, sed -n 'A,Bp')
- read(path, offset, limit): read a file with line numbers

Rules:
- Answer ONLY from text you have actually read in this session. Do not answer from memory.
- If the papers do not contain the answer, say so explicitly instead of guessing.
- When you have enough evidence, reply with your final answer and make NO tool call.
- Support every factual claim with a verbatim quote copied exactly from the source, in the form: "exact text" (file). Never paraphrase inside the quotation marks. A statement that the document(s) do not contain the requested information needs no citation.
- State only what the document(s) say. Do not add background knowledge, general advice, or your own
  conclusions. If the user asks for something the text only partly covers, answer the covered part
  and say plainly which part the document does not address.
- After you give an answer, an automatic check verifies your citations. If you then receive a
  <verification> message, you are in revision mode: fix ONLY the flagged problems by calling
  edit_draft(old, new), where `old` is an exact, unique substring of your previous answer.
  Keep everything else unchanged, and reply "Done" when finished.
  Never call edit_draft before you have given an answer.

What are some tips on saving money?

In your answer, refer only to the document in the file `doc.txt`. Do not employ any outside knowledge.

1	Money Management Tips: 55 Ways to Save Money
     2	Recreation and Entertainment:
     3	1. Instead of paying for a fitness club
     4	membership fee, buy some weights or go to
     5	the ARC.
     6	2. Don’t smoke. Cigarettes are expensive and
     7	the money adds up quickly. Also you’ll be
     8	fined if you smoke near school facilities.
     9	3. Wait until after half-time at sport events
    10	and get in for free!
    11	4. When eating out, look for coupons or
    12	special deals- many restaurants offer them!
    13	Also, order water. Drinks are highly
    14	overpriced.
    15	5. At the beginning of the semester, many
    16	local businesses give out coupon books.
    17	Grab one!
    18	6. There are hundreds of free activities on
    19	campus. Join clubs, attend student
    20	concerts, or go to church-sponsored events
    21	for cheap fun. There is usually food
    22	involved, too!
    23	7. Illinites, student activities, happen at the
    24	Illini Union every Friday night for free.
    25	8. Experience some more cultures while in
    26	college and attend a show at Krannert.
    27	Student tickets are $10 or less. It’s FREE
    28	sometimes!
    29	9. If you’re throwing a party, have your guests
    30	pay a little money or bring things to offset
    31	your cost.
    32	10. Don’t purchase a book unless you think you
    33	really want to keep it. You can check out
    34	books for free at libraries.
    35	11. Rent movies with a group of friends or go to
    36	second-run theaters for $1 or $2 a ticket.
    37	12. Bring your student ID when you go out for a
    38	movie. Most theaters will give discount for
    39	students.
    40	
    41	Food and Basic Needs:
    42	13. Be a savvy consumer. Before making a
    43	major purchase, do some researches on the
    44	product quality through Consumer Reports
    45	magazine.
    46	14. Sometimes the cheaper product works just
    47	as well as the expensive one.
    48	15. Ask for generic medications at the
    49	pharmacy.
    50	16. Ladies, ditch the salon and get your hair
    51	done at a cosmetology school.
    52	17. Buying in bulk is usually a good option, but
    53	try to shop for items by the per unit price.
    54	Often times, the biggest options is not the
    55	best way to get the most of your money.
    56	18. Scout out garage/yard sales for
    57	housewares, furniture, and stuff to
    58	decorate your college dorm or apartment.
    59	At the beginning of each semester, the
    60	YMCA has a dump and run where they sell
    61	items collected from various dorms and
    62	apartment on campus.
    63	19. Make things for gifts- it’s cheaper and the
    64	time you invest shows you care.
    65	20. Take advantage of sales by buying holiday
    66	and birthday gifts throughout the year.
    67	21. Get a job at a place where you already
    68	spend a lot of money, so you can get
    69	employee discounts.
    70	22. Use mail-in rebates or coupons for groceries
    71	or health and beauty items.
    72	23. Don’t buy bottled water. Buy a water
    73	filtration pitcher.
    74	24. Don’t buy something just because it is one
    75	sale. Consider it’s a need for you before
    76	buying.
    77	25. If you shop at a favorite store, apply for
    78	their discount card if they have one.
    79	
    80	Modified by Joe Pleshar, Yuanhang Fan, and Maggie Benson, Peer Educators of Spring 2015.
    81	University of Illinois Extension Financial Wellness for College Students Program.
    82	Source: National Student Loan Program’s Budget Handout #6: “Money Management
    83	Options: 75 Ways to Save Money”, 2002.
    84	
    85	
    86	Money Management Tips: 55 Ways to Save Money
    87	26. Make home cooked meals. A home cooked
    88	stead dinner is often cheaper than a fast
    89	food binge. Eating at home will save you a
    90	lot of money!
    91	27. Pack a lunch instead of eating out.
    92	
    93	Clothing:
    94	28. Buy clothes at the end of the season when
    95	they’re on sales.
    96	29. If you don’t wear certain clothes anymore,
    97	take them to a consignment shop or sell
    98	them online. You can get part of the profit
    99	and free up room in your closet.
   100	30. Share dresses and tuxes with friends for
   101	special occasions.
   102	31. If you buy more than one of something, like
   103	2 or 3 shirts, always ask for a discount.
   104	32. Invest in durable clothes, shoes, etc. rather
   105	than buying many cheap pairs.
   106	
   107	Budgeting/ Spending Plan:
   108	33. Set goals for your spending and saving.
   109	34. Keep track of your spending to avoid
   110	overspent. There are apps for that!
   111	35. Don’t use a credit card if it will lead you to
   112	make more purchases! On average, people
   113	have credit cards spend 34% more.
   114	36. Before going out to spend, set a limit for
   115	yourself and stick to it!
   116	37. Wait at least two hours before making a big
   117	purchase to be sure it’s something you
   118	really need.
   119	
   120	Transportation:
   121	38. Obey traffic laws. Speeding tickets will cost
   122	more than just the ticket. It will raise your
   123	insurance premiums.
   124	39. Keep your tires inflated properly- you’ll get
   125	better gas mileage.
   126	
   127	40. Get good grades. Insurance companies offer
   128	low rates to student with 3.0+ GPA.
   129	41. Carpool with friend!
   130	42. Search for dependable cards that offer good
   131	gas mileage.
   132	43. Drive an older car- the insurance payments
   133	and taxes will be less.
   134	44. Walk, bike, or ride to school- it’s good for
   135	you to saves on gas.
   136	45. Look around for cheapest gas price before
   137	filling up. There are apps for that!
   138	
   139	Savings:
   140	46. Only use ATM’s of your bank. Other bank’s
   141	ATM fees add up!
   142	47. Always put part of our paycheck into a
   143	savings account.
   144	48. Spare change adds up! Get a piggy bank or
   145	change jar and don’t underestimate the
   146	value of your spare changes.
   147	49. Volunteer! If you’re busy, you can’t spend
   148	month and it’s a resume booster, too! It’s
   149	always make you feel good to help and give
   150	back to the community.
   151	50. Use plastic grocery bags for trash can liners.
   152	
   153	Conserving Resources:
   154	51. Turn off the water while brushing your
   155	teeth.
   156	52. Unplug electronics when you aren’t using
   157	them. Even while turned off, they still use
   158	up costly energy.
   159	53. Use items like shampoo, toothpaste, and
   160	paper towels sparingly- enough to do the
   161	job without waste.
   162	54. Pay your bills online. Save paper and money
   163	on stamps.
   164	55. Ask your landlord to seal gaps between
   165	door and windows to prevent heat leaks
   166	over the winter.
   167	
   168	Modified by Joe Pleshar, Yuanhang Fan, and Maggie Benson, Peer Educators of Spring 2015.
   169	University of Illinois Extension Financial Wellness for College Students Program.
   170	Source: National Student Loan Program’s Budget Handout #6: “Money Management
   171	Options: 75 Ways to Save Money”, 2002.
